> Verify that different parsers used in the application for the same data type
(e.g., JSON parsers, XML parsers, URL parsers), perform parsing in a
consistent way and use the same character encoding mechanism to avoid
issues such as JSON Interoperability vulnerabilities or different URI or file
parsing behavior being exploited in Remote File Inclusion (RFI) or
Server‑side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

For many data types, there is no single industry standard for "**consistent**" different implementations make different valid choices. Discovering every single implicit and explicit parser across a **large, multi-language, microservices architecture is nearly impossible**.

comments.body: I see this requirement as more of functionality vs security and suggest we delete it. RFI and SSRF are well covered elsewhere.

I don't agree with the deletion proposal. It is an L3 defense-in-depth requirement and has its place in the standard.

If the "functionality" does not work correctly, it may provide a bypass from validation rules or cause data integrity problems.

RFI and SSRF are potential outcomes for URI parsing problems, as examples, and are not the main goal for the requirement.

> If the "functionality" does not work correctly, it may provide a bypass from validation rules or cause data integrity problems.


How does this functionality work correctly in a microservice environment? I agree that ASVS is not responsible for providing implementation details, I believe microservice use cases may have been missed when drafting the requirement.

I would suggest to redraft the requirement and the security goal remain same.

title: Clarification: 1.5.3 "consistent"
